correctness.rationale: Every facet normal is a sign vector supported on a maximal chain, so its norm is the square root of that chain's cardinality. For an arbitrary ball center, maximizing the signed facet functional gives the sum of absolute center coordinates along the chain, yielding the exact feasibility condition and complete incenter set. A longest chain gives the universal upper bound and the origin attains it. The uniqueness criterion is proved in both directions. For the outer radius, every generator is a signed antichain vector of norm at most the square root of the width; a maximum antichain gives an antipodal pair attaining that bound. Equality in the Euclidean triangle inequality gives the complete outer contact set. No finite computation is used as proof.

value.rationale: Height and width are the two basic extremal order parameters of a finite poset. The theorem recovers them exactly as the reciprocal squared inradius and squared circumradius of a canonical poset polytope, and further identifies all optimal centers and both inner and outer contact structures. This is a family-wide structural metric interpretation, not a finite table or arbitrary parameter slice. The nonpure case produces a substantive uniqueness phenomenon: the incenter is unique exactly when longest chains cover the ground set.
